title: The Royal Test of Four Noble Virtues (TA)
summary: Akbar tests four young noble candidates for governorship. Birbal arranges four secret trials to reveal their true character. [TA]
full_text:
Four young noble princes competed for the prestigious appointment of Governor of the wealthy province of Gujarat. Each candidate was polished, eloquent, and presented glowing letters of recommendation from high ministers.

Emperor Akbar was unsure whom to choose: 'Birbal, all four speak like angels! How can I know which one will govern with genuine justice?'

Birbal smiled: 'Sire, let us test them not with examinations of words, but with secret trials of action.'

Birbal arranged four secret scenarios along the road as the four candidates traveled to the palace for their final interview.

Candidate One passed an old woman whose cart was stuck in a ditch. He ignored her, saying: 'I cannot soil my silk coat; I must meet the Emperor!'

Candidate Two found a leather purse containing fifty gold coins dropped on the trail. He pocketed the gold in secret, whispering: 'A lucky windfall!'

Candidate Three encountered a wounded stray dog whining in pain. He kicked the animal aside to clear his path.

Candidate Four, named Prince Vijay, saw the stuck cart, dismounted his horse, rolled up his sleeves, and helped the old woman push her cart free. When he found an iron ring dropped in the mud, he handed it to the village watchman. And when he saw the wounded dog, he bound its paw with his own silk handkerchief and left water for the beast.

When the four candidates assembled before the throne, Akbar was about to begin the interview when Birbal stepped forward, accompanied by the old woman, the watchman, and the bandaged dog!

Birbal revealed the secret trials:

'Sire, governance is tested in the shadows, not on the stage!

'A man who will not help a stuck cart will never help a starving peasant. A man who steals a purse in the dark will embezzle your provincial revenues. And a man who kicks a wounded animal will be a cruel tyrant to his subjects!

'Only Prince Vijay passed every test of compassion, honesty, and mercy. He alone possesses the noble character to govern Gujarat!'

Akbar appointed Prince Vijay Governor on the spot, praising Birbal for proving that secret deeds reveal the true soul of a ruler.
moral: நீதி மற்றும் வாழ்க்கை பாடம்: Wit beats power
